title: PrePay Power (Prepaid Metering) Worksheet Note: Opening Daily Cost From the Year's Billing History
content:
This note sets the opening daily cost used for the PrePay Power (Prepaid Metering) activation payment from the standard billing history of the enrolled service account on Electric Service by Rate Schedule: its standard bills and their usage lines.

**Clause.** Where the enrolled service account carries at least 12 standard bills in the twelve-month window, the opening daily cost is the larger of the total of the usage lines of the most recent bill and the total of the usage lines dated in the thirteen-month window but not in the twelve-month window, divided by 30. Where it carries at least 6 but fewer than 12 standard bills in the twelve-month window, the opening daily cost is the total of the usage lines in the six-month window divided by 182. An account in any other situation keeps the most recent bill's daily cost.

**Defined terms.**

1. *Month window.* A month window of a stated number of months covers the records dated after the same day of the month that many months before the current date, up to and including the current date.
2. *Standard bills in the twelve-month window.* The standard bills of the enrolled service account dated within that window.
3. *Usage lines dated in the thirteen-month window but not in the twelve-month window.* The usage lines of the records dated within the thirteen-month window that fall before the start of the twelve-month window.
4. *The larger of.* The two totals are compared first; only the larger is divided by 30.

### Worked figures (hypothetical histories)

| Bills in the twelve-month window | Most recent bill's usage lines | Usage lines dated between thirteen and twelve months back | Six-month usage lines | Opening daily cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 12 | 140.00 | 186.00 | | 186.00 divided by 30, which is 6.20 |
| 12 | 210.00 | 150.00 | | 210.00 divided by 30, which is 7.00 |
| 8 | 165.00 | | 728.00 | 728.00 divided by 182, which is 4.00 |
| 5 | 120.00 | | | keeps the most recent bill's daily cost |

Boundary: 11 bills falls in the six-month row and 12 bills in the first row; 6 bills is the lowest count of the six-month row.
